title: Coulomb's Law
principle: Electrostatic force between point charges scales with charge product and inverse-square separation.
applicability_conditions: Charges are approximated as point charges or spherically symmetric
Medium is uniform, commonly vacuum in introductory form
Electrostatic regime with negligible radiation effects

limiting_cases.result: Point-charge model predicts divergence and breaks down physically.

misconceptions.wrong_model: Like charges attract if one charge is much larger.
misconceptions.correction: Sign determines attraction or repulsion; magnitude only changes force size.
Inverse-square scaling means doubling distance reduces force to one quarter.

historical_context: Formulated by Charles-Augustin de Coulomb in the 1780s using torsion balance experiments.
description: The electric force between two point charges scales with charge product and falls with inverse-square distance.

idealizations.name: Material medium
idealizations.note: The vacuum form is emphasized before introducing dielectric effects.

author: austin
subject: physics

title: Electric Field (F = qE)
principle: Electric field gives force per unit positive test charge at each point in space.

limiting_cases.result: Test-force tends to zero while field remains defined by source charges.

description: Electric field describes how strongly and in what direction charges would be pushed at each point in space.

idealizations.name: Polarization effects
idealizations.note: Intro field definitions assume simple media or vacuum behavior.

author: austin
subject: physics

title: Ohm's Law (I = V/R)
principle: For ohmic conductors, current is proportional to voltage with resistance as proportionality constant.
applicability_conditions: Conductor operates in approximately linear ohmic regime
Temperature is approximately constant
Steady-state circuit conditions apply

limiting_cases.result: Ideal short-circuit behavior with very large current for finite voltage.
Open-circuit behavior with current approaching zero.

misconceptions.wrong_model: Current is consumed by a resistor.
misconceptions.correction: Charge flow is continuous; resistors dissipate energy, not charge.

misconceptions.wrong_model: Voltage is a flowing substance in wires.
misconceptions.correction: Voltage is a potential difference; current is what flows.

historical_context: Georg Ohm published this relationship in 1827, initially meeting significant skepticism.
description: In many conductors, voltage is proportional to current with resistance as the proportionality constant.

idealizations.name: Temperature
idealizations.note: Resistance is treated as constant in the linear ohmic regime.

author: austin
subject: physics

title: Faraday's Law of Induction
principle: Changing magnetic flux through a loop induces an emf opposing the change.
applicability_conditions: Magnetic flux through a conducting loop changes over time
Loop orientation and area are well-defined
Macroscopic classical electromagnetism applies
description: A changing magnetic flux induces an emf, which drives current in a closed loop.

idealizations.name: Circuit resistance
idealizations.note: The flux-emf relation is introduced independent of resistive details.

author: austin
subject: physics

title: Gauss's Law
principle: Electric flux through a closed surface equals enclosed charge divided by vacuum permittivity.
applicability_conditions: Closed Gaussian surface is defined
Field and charge distribution satisfy electrostatic modeling assumptions
Symmetry is used when solving for explicit field magnitudes

limiting_cases.result: Net electric flux through the closed surface is zero.

misconceptions.wrong_model: Only charges located on the surface contribute to flux.
misconceptions.correction: Only net enclosed charge determines total flux, regardless of exact placement inside.

misconceptions.wrong_model: Zero net flux means electric field is zero everywhere on the surface.
misconceptions.correction: Field can be nonzero locally while positive and negative contributions cancel in net flux.

historical_context: Integral law developed by Carl Friedrich Gauss and became foundational to Maxwell's framework.
description: Total electric flux through a closed surface equals enclosed charge divided by vacuum permittivity.

idealizations.name: Symmetry imperfections
idealizations.note: Canonical examples assume ideal geometric symmetry for tractable flux integrals.
